newsitem.title: UK: IPE futures trade at contract highs on Iraq move.
newsitem.headline: IPE futures trade at contract highs on Iraq move.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures gained $1 on Monday and gas oil consolidated five-year highs as the market digested news that it would be living without Iraqi crude longer than earlier anticipated.
October Brent was at 1458 GMT trading up 95 cents from Friday's close at $21.73 a barrel, five cents below a contract high of $21.78 achieved in the morning session.

With the New York market closed for the Labor Day holiday, IPE Brent took the initiative and firmed on the strength of a U.N. decision to delay implementation of the oil-for-food deal after Iraqi troops moved into the Kurdish northern regions.
"The real reason we are up is of course that we are now going to be living without Iraqi oil a bit longer than whatever time frame anyone had put on it before," a crude broker said.
Latest reports from Kurdistan said Iraqi troops were pulling out of Arbil, the capital of Iraqi Kurdistan but opponents of President Saddam Hussein reported executions in the streets.
IPE Sept gas oil also rose on the back of crude, reaching a session high of $206 a tonne before drifting back to $205.25, up $8.50.
Dutch inspectors Saybolt said plans to send experts to monitor food sales in Iraq had been suspended for now.

Under a deal with the U.N. in May, Iraq had been expected to start exporting crude worth $2 billion over six months to pay for food and medicines for the first time since the 1990 U.N. embargo after its invasion of Kuwait.

U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali responded to Iraq's move into Iraqi Kurdistan by delaying the deployment in northern Iraq of U.N. personnel to supervise aid distribution under the oil for food plan.
Iraq amassed 30,000-40,000 troops in northern Kurdish provinces and captured Arbil at the weekend, expelling one Kurdish faction and installing a rival group.
